# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The incumbent passes simulation and has routed setup and hold slack of 0.554 ns and 0.063 ns, respectively, so timing is feasible. At 42 LUTs and 90 FFs, it has no objective improvement yet. The top’s numeric latency is unknown; preserve its cycle behavior without inventing a top latency annotation.

## Hypothesis

Deriving the register file’s write enable from the registered one-hot grant may remove one redundant FF while keeping LUT use at or below 42, improving the `(LUTs, FFs)` objective if LUT count stays equal.

## Instruction for generator

Remove the arbiter’s registered `wr_en` state and derive the register file write enable from the registered grant being nonzero; retain the registered write address and data. Preserve the one-cycle registered write channel behavior, including idle cycles and synchronous reset blocking writes, as well as round-robin grant behavior and read-first memory behavior. Check routed LUT and FF counts, WNS and WHS, and require every deterministic verification gate to pass before accepting the candidate.
